world.title: Saudi Arabia delays flagship investment summit until 2027 after Houthi attacks
world.summary: Saudi Arabia has postponed its Future Investment Initiative (FII), the kingdom’s flagship investment conference, from Oct. 26-29 to 2027 over security concerns following Houthi attacks; a new date has not been set. The event’s 10th edition was expected to draw global business leaders and financiers to Riyadh. The state
world.content: Saudi Arabia has postponed its Future Investment Initiative (FII), the kingdom’s flagship investment conference, from Oct. 26-29 to 2027 over security concerns following Houthi attacks; a new date has not been set. The event’s 10th edition was expected to draw global business leaders and financiers to Riyadh. The state-backed gathering promotes Saudi efforts to attract foreign capital and diversify its economy beyond hydrocarbons into tourism, sports and technology. Recent Houthi strikes have hit military, energy and civilian sites, including Riyadh’s airport, disrupting travel. Semafor reported that banks and private-equity firms had privately raised safety concerns with Public Investment Fund Governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan. Organizers said the conference would return in 2027, with revised dates to be announced soon. The FII Institute said it wanted the 10th edition to retain its expected scale and quality. Other Saudi events have also been postponed, including Intersec Saudi Arabia, now scheduled for October 2027, and the Saudi Retail Forum, moved to March 2027.

world.title: Cost-of-living protests spread across Europe as France reports 2,400 arrests
world.summary: Protests over living costs, housing, schools and public services have spread across France, Italy, Albania, Spain, Portugal and Belgium, with looting and clashes in several cities. The demonstrations have no single organizing body and reflect distinct national grievances, including education funding in France, housing
world.content: Protests over living costs, housing, schools and public services have spread across France, Italy, Albania, Spain, Portugal and Belgium, with looting and clashes in several cities. The demonstrations have no single organizing body and reflect distinct national grievances, including education funding in France, housing costs in Spain and Portugal, and corruption allegations in Albania. In France, a student campaign for more school resources broadened into nationwide demonstrations over prices and public services. Authorities reported about 2,400 arrests after the Oct. 17 protests, which included looting, fires and clashes with police; hundreds were injured. President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence, while unions and protesters criticized the police response and the government’s handling of their grievances. A national strike and demonstrations are planned in France for Nov. 5, Italy’s Oct. 17 Movement has called for weekly Saturday protests, and Serbia holds parliamentary elections on Oct. 25 amid a student-led anti-corruption movement. In Spain, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called a snap election for November after affordable-housing measures failed to win parliamentary support.
world.image_alt: Cost-of-living protests spread across Europe as France reports 2,400 arrests

world.title: Houthi missiles kill 53 recruits at Yemen security training camp
world.summary: Houthi forces struck the al-Alam security training camp in Yemen’s Shabwa province with three ballistic missiles on Monday, killing at least 53 recruits and wounding more than 200, according to local authorities. The Houthis acknowledged the attack, saying they targeted Saudi-backed forces at the camp; Yemeni officials
world.content: Houthi forces struck the al-Alam security training camp in Yemen’s Shabwa province with three ballistic missiles on Monday, killing at least 53 recruits and wounding more than 200, according to local authorities. The Houthis acknowledged the attack, saying they targeted Saudi-backed forces at the camp; Yemeni officials said the recruits were training for internal security duties. The Houthis advanced toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in September, and forces of the internationally recognized, Saudi-backed government launched a counteroffensive this month to retake coastal territory. The renewed fighting has broken a 2022 truce that had largely halted major combat. Hospitals in Shabwa were overwhelmed, and the most seriously wounded were transferred to facilities in neighboring Hadramout and Aden. Shabwa authorities urged the government and Saudi-led coalition to provide air defenses and early-warning systems; Rashad al-Alimi, president of Yemen’s internationally recognized government, pledged a firm response.
world.image_alt: Houthi missiles kill 53 recruits at Yemen security training camp

world.title: Trump urges Ukraine to choose another negotiator as Kyiv alleges missile delays
world.summary: President Donald Trump said Monday that Ukraine should choose someone other than President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to negotiate with Russia, while Zelenskyy accused the United States of delaying European-funded Patriot interceptor missiles. Washington also recently eased sanctions on Moscow tied to Russian diesel supplies.
world.content: President Donald Trump said Monday that Ukraine should choose someone other than President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to negotiate with Russia, while Zelenskyy accused the United States of delaying European-funded Patriot interceptor missiles. Washington also recently eased sanctions on Moscow tied to Russian diesel supplies. Zelenskyy told U.S. senators that one missile shipment was awaiting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s approval and that European countries also needed U.S. authorization to transfer Patriot missiles from their own stockpiles. He said Ukraine had received no advance warning of Russian attacks on three occasions in the past week; Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that Washington had paused intelligence sharing. Trump defended his approach and accused Zelenskyy of obstructing a settlement. Zelenskyy said Kyiv would halt attacks on Russian oil refineries for 30 days if Washington supplied the interceptors. U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff is expected in Norway this week for talks involving Zelenskyy and European partners, including the United Kingdom, France, Germany and Poland, as well as the European Union and NATO.
world.image_alt: Trump urges Ukraine to choose another negotiator as Kyiv alleges missile delays

world.title: Trump says he is willing to meet Putin and Xi for nuclear talks
world.summary: President Donald Trump said Oct. 19 he would join Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping for a three-way meeting in China if Xi agrees, with nuclear weapons and denuclearization as the main topics. The leaders could meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shen
world.content: President Donald Trump said Oct. 19 he would join Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping for a three-way meeting in China if Xi agrees, with nuclear weapons and denuclearization as the main topics. The leaders could meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on Nov. 18-19, but the Kremlin said there had been no substantive proposals or agreements. Putin reportedly suggested using the meeting to discuss ending Russia’s war in Ukraine on terms favorable to Moscow, while Trump said he wanted to focus on arms control and renewed his criticism of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The proposed format does not include Kyiv. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said a meeting without Ukraine could encourage Putin to continue the war, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said a final settlement requires Kyiv’s participation. Beijing has long opposed joining nuclear talks with Washington and Moscow, whose arsenals are much larger. The New START treaty, the last remaining U.S.-Russian nuclear arms pact, expired in February, leaving no legally binding nuclear arms framework between the two countries. China has said it considers calls to join trilateral disarmament talks unfair and unrealistic.
world.image_alt: Trump says he is willing to meet Putin and Xi for nuclear talks

world.title: Japan launches probe to collect Phobos samples for 2031 return
world.summary: Japan launched its Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft on Oct. 20, beginning a five-year mission to study Mars’ moons and return samples from Phobos, the larger of the two. The probe separated from an H3 rocket about 71 minutes after liftoff from Tanegashima Space Center, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (
world.content: Japan launched its Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft on Oct. 20, beginning a five-year mission to study Mars’ moons and return samples from Phobos, the larger of the two. The probe separated from an H3 rocket about 71 minutes after liftoff from Tanegashima Space Center, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) said. MMX is designed to collect at least 10 grams of material to investigate whether Phobos and Deimos formed from debris after a collision with Mars or are asteroids captured by the planet’s gravity. Scientists also expect Phobos to contain traces of material blasted from Mars’ surface by impacts. The spacecraft is scheduled to reach Mars in August 2027, deploy a French-German rover to survey Phobos and then attempt to collect samples before leaving the Martian system in 2030. Its return capsule is expected to land in Australia in 2031.
world.image_alt: Japan launches probe to collect Phobos samples for 2031 return

world.title: Australian MP loses leg after suspected deliberate car ramming
world.summary: Independent Australian lawmaker Helen Haines lost a leg after a driver allegedly rammed her with a Toyota Land Cruiser outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Oct. 19. The 65-year-old remained in critical but stable condition in a Melbourne hospital on Tuesday as surgeons worked to save her other leg,
world.content: Independent Australian lawmaker Helen Haines lost a leg after a driver allegedly rammed her with a Toyota Land Cruiser outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Oct. 19. The 65-year-old remained in critical but stable condition in a Melbourne hospital on Tuesday as surgeons worked to save her other leg, according to local media reports. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said witnesses described the driver making a U-turn before striking Haines. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said witnesses reported that the vehicle reversed and hit her a second time. A bystander, barber Ricky Jefferies, helped restrain the driver, and police found a knife in the vehicle. The 43-year-old suspect remained in custody as federal and Victoria state police and counterterrorism investigators worked to establish a motive and determine possible charges. No motive had been confirmed, and police said the incident appeared isolated, with no known further threats connected to it.

world.title: Unlicensed Colombian gold mine collapse kills 14, injures seven
world.summary: A collapse at an unlicensed open-pit gold mine near Santa Bárbara de Iscuandé in Colombia’s Nariño department killed 14 people and injured seven on Monday, Oct. 19. Search operations have ended. Four of the injured were in serious condition, and the Nariño governor’s office worked with the army to arrange their evacuat
world.content: A collapse at an unlicensed open-pit gold mine near Santa Bárbara de Iscuandé in Colombia’s Nariño department killed 14 people and injured seven on Monday, Oct. 19. Search operations have ended. Four of the injured were in serious condition, and the Nariño governor’s office worked with the army to arrange their evacuation by air to Tumaco. Rescuers faced difficult terrain and the presence of armed criminal groups in the remote area, which is accessible only by boat or small aircraft. Illegal gold mining is a major source of income for armed groups in Nariño, alongside drug trafficking and extortion, and the regional government says communities have few economic alternatives. The collapse was the second fatal mine disaster in Nariño in less than three months: 13 people died in a similar accident in August. Nariño Governor Luis Alfonso Escobar has urged the national government, the National Mining Agency and the Mines and Energy Ministry to speed up the formalization of small-scale mining to improve safety.

business.title: Canadian inflation reaches 3.1% as gasoline prices jump 27.8%
business.summary: Canada’s annual inflation rate rose to 3.1% in September from 3.0% in August, driven mainly by gasoline prices that climbed 27.8% year over year; excluding gasoline, inflation eased to 2.2% from 2.4%. Energy prices rose 19% year over year, while fuel oil and other fuels surged 57.8%. Underlying inflation measures eased
business.content: Canada’s annual inflation rate rose to 3.1% in September from 3.0% in August, driven mainly by gasoline prices that climbed 27.8% year over year; excluding gasoline, inflation eased to 2.2% from 2.4%. Energy prices rose 19% year over year, while fuel oil and other fuels surged 57.8%. Underlying inflation measures eased, but Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem has warned that prolonged high energy costs could spread inflation more broadly. Economists said the report alone did not make an interest-rate increase urgent. The bank’s next rate decision is scheduled for Oct. 28. Statistics Canada will publish October’s inflation figures on Nov. 16.
business.image_alt: Canadian inflation reaches 3.1% as gasoline prices jump 27.8%

business.title: Jio Platforms draws $26.3 billion in bids before $3.2 billion IPO
business.summary: Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital-services arm of Reliance Industries, attracted bids worth 2.5 trillion rupees ($26.3 billion) for its 81.1 billion-rupee ($854 million) anchor allocation, more than 30 times the amount available, ahead of its public offering opening Oct. 21. It allotted 72.47 million shares to 212
business.content: Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital-services arm of Reliance Industries, attracted bids worth 2.5 trillion rupees ($26.3 billion) for its 81.1 billion-rupee ($854 million) anchor allocation, more than 30 times the amount available, ahead of its public offering opening Oct. 21. It allotted 72.47 million shares to 212 anchor investors at 1,119 rupees apiece, the top of its price range. The IPO aims to raise 30,213 crore rupees ($3.2 billion), valuing Jio at about $108 billion. The offering of newly issued shares runs through Oct. 23. Jio plans to use much of the proceeds to repay borrowings at its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm, and the rest for general corporate purposes. Reliance Industries will retain majority ownership after the listing. The anchor bids are indicative, not committed capital.

business.title: CoreWeave debt strain fuels warnings over AI infrastructure spending
business.summary: CoreWeave, a U.S. provider of computing capacity for artificial intelligence, saw its bonds enter distressed territory last week as investors questioned whether AI services revenue can support the sector’s borrowing and data-center investment. The company reported more than $35 billion in debt in its second-quarter res
business.content: CoreWeave, a U.S. provider of computing capacity for artificial intelligence, saw its bonds enter distressed territory last week as investors questioned whether AI services revenue can support the sector’s borrowing and data-center investment. The company reported more than $35 billion in debt in its second-quarter results and lost more than $1 billion in the first half of 2026, while its shares fell about 25% last week. Gartner forecast that more than $3.5 trillion in planned AI infrastructure investment could face impairment by 2030 and that 80% of neocloud computing providers may not remain independent as spending outpaces profitable demand. Oracle, another heavily indebted AI infrastructure business, saw its shares fall nearly 10% over the same period. Gartner chief forecaster John Lovelock said excess computing capacity and free AI services are limiting returns.
business.image_alt: CoreWeave debt strain fuels warnings over AI infrastructure spending

business.title: US bars DeepSeek AI from civilian agencies over security risks
business.summary: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products and third-party services built with the Chinese AI company’s models, and barred agencies from acquiring those tools. DHS issued the order July 24 and made it public Monday. It applies to departments including Tr
business.content: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products and third-party services built with the Chinese AI company’s models, and barred agencies from acquiring those tools. DHS issued the order July 24 and made it public Monday. It applies to departments including Treasury, State and Justice but excludes the Defense Department; DHS’s authority does not extend to military or intelligence agencies. DHS warned that government employees or vendors using the tools could transfer sensitive data to China and expose agencies to malware or other security vulnerabilities. The directive extends earlier agency restrictions across civilian agencies. Separately, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) is scheduled to vote Oct. 29 on whether to bar Chinese testing labs from testing electronic devices for U.S. use.
business.image_alt: US bars DeepSeek AI from civilian agencies over security risks

business.title: Saudi Arabia delays investor summit as firms flag travel risks
business.summary: Saudi Arabia postponed its Future Investment Initiative (FII), the kingdom’s flagship investment conference, in Riyadh until 2027 as banks and private-equity firms privately raised concerns with Saudi Public Investment Fund Governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan about the safety of attending. The in-person event, scheduled for Oct
business.content: Saudi Arabia postponed its Future Investment Initiative (FII), the kingdom’s flagship investment conference, in Riyadh until 2027 as banks and private-equity firms privately raised concerns with Saudi Public Investment Fund Governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan about the safety of attending. The in-person event, scheduled for Oct. 26-29, is a state-backed platform for pitching investment plans and attracting capital to diversify the economy beyond hydrocarbons. JPMorgan Chase chief executive Jamie Dimon, BlackRock chief Larry Fink and Goldman Sachs chief executive David Solomon were among the global finance and corporate leaders expected to attend. Organizers had considered a hybrid format that would let executives participate remotely, but announced the conference would move to 2027. The security situation has also affected ordinary business operations in Riyadh: government agencies told staff to work remotely for part of the week, while companies in the King Abdullah Financial District asked employees to stay home. Organizers said new conference dates would be announced soon.
business.image_alt: Saudi Arabia delays investor summit as firms flag travel risks

business.title: US judge keeps former OpenAI engineer detained over alleged office bugging
business.summary: A federal magistrate judge in San Francisco on Oct. 19 ordered former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan held without bail, finding a significant risk that he would not return to court. Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi citizen and U.S. permanent resident, faces one charge of using or attempting to use a device to intercep
business.content: A federal magistrate judge in San Francisco on Oct. 19 ordered former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan held without bail, finding a significant risk that he would not return to court. Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi citizen and U.S. permanent resident, faces one charge of using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications. He has not been charged with espionage or acting for a foreign government. Prosecutors allege he placed an audio recorder behind a television in an OpenAI executive conference room on Sept. 28, where executives and government officials met. They say evidence suggests he considered installing other devices. They cited his contacts with an unnamed Saudi royal, plans to travel to Riyadh and alleged Saudi-linked assistance for his family as reasons he could flee. The defense says he planned the trip for family and immigration reasons and disputes that he intended to leave permanently. OpenAI has said it found no indication that Alfozan improperly accessed or removed model weights, source code or customer data. Prosecutors say the investigation remains active and additional charges are possible. Alfozan’s next hearing is scheduled for Nov. 6.
business.image_alt: US judge keeps former OpenAI engineer detained over alleged office bugging

business.title: AI market sell-off exposes debt risks as earnings tests begin
business.summary: Shares linked to artificial intelligence and credit markets came under pressure last week as investors questioned whether heavy spending on data centers and chips will generate returns. The Nasdaq 100 fell 5.5% before technology shares rebounded on Monday. Investors are assessing a projected $1 trillion in AI investmen
business.content: Shares linked to artificial intelligence and credit markets came under pressure last week as investors questioned whether heavy spending on data centers and chips will generate returns. The Nasdaq 100 fell 5.5% before technology shares rebounded on Monday. Investors are assessing a projected $1 trillion in AI investment this year, while credit concerns have spread beyond smaller infrastructure providers to large technology borrowers. Investors are concerned that revenues may depend too heavily on spending within the AI industry and that rising borrowing costs could weaken debt-financed projects. CoreWeave’s bonds have yielded as much as 15%, while Oracle’s credit-default-swap spread rose sharply, drawing scrutiny of its rating at the lowest investment-grade level. Analysts disagree on whether the pullback is a valuation reset or a warning that expected returns may fall short. BlackRock Chief Executive Larry Fink has argued that compute and energy shortages are a greater constraint than a bubble. Meta and Tesla are scheduled to report third-quarter results on Oct. 21, followed by Alphabet and Microsoft on Oct. 29 and Amazon on Oct. 30.
business.image_alt: AI market sell-off exposes debt risks as earnings tests begin

business.title: Indonesia targets stocks with concentrated ownership after MSCI downgrade threat
business.summary: Indonesia’s stock exchange said it would remove companies with highly concentrated ownership from its benchmark index as authorities responded to MSCI’s proposal to downgrade the country from emerging-market to standalone status. MSCI cited persistent opacity in shareholdings, suspected coordinated trading and weak enf
business.content: Indonesia’s stock exchange said it would remove companies with highly concentrated ownership from its benchmark index as authorities responded to MSCI’s proposal to downgrade the country from emerging-market to standalone status. MSCI cited persistent opacity in shareholdings, suspected coordinated trading and weak enforcement. The Jakarta Composite Index fell 11.6% on Friday and another 3.6% on Monday, closing at a six-year low of 4,996. Stocks rebounded about 3% on Tuesday after officials announced measures to improve transparency and price discovery, but the rupiah remained near its record low, at around 18,030 per dollar. Foreign investors have sold about $5 billion of Indonesian shares this year, while analysts warn a downgrade could prompt further outflows and spread to government bonds. The exchange says it will disclose whether investors holding at least 1% of a listed company are affiliated with that company. Shares with concentrated ownership account for about 18% of the Jakarta index’s weight. MSCI is collecting market feedback through April 2027 and plans to decide by June 30. Bank Indonesia is due to announce its rate decision on Wednesday, Oct. 21, with analysts divided over whether it will raise rates to support the rupiah.
business.image_alt: Indonesia targets stocks with concentrated ownership after MSCI downgrade threat

science.title: NASA rover captures wind-carved Martian cliffs in dawn panorama
science.summary: NASA’s Curiosity rover has sent back a detailed dawn panorama of wind-carved cliffs on Mount Sharp that scientists aim to examine up close. The ridges, called yardangs, stretch about 10 miles (16 kilometers) across the mountain’s northwestern flank. Their unusual color and tilted layers leave their origin uncertain; on
science.content: NASA’s Curiosity rover has sent back a detailed dawn panorama of wind-carved cliffs on Mount Sharp that scientists aim to examine up close. The ridges, called yardangs, stretch about 10 miles (16 kilometers) across the mountain’s northwestern flank. Their unusual color and tilted layers leave their origin uncertain; one possibility is ancient volcanic ash. Curiosity took the six images on Aug. 11, and the team released them without the usual white-balance adjustment, preserving the scene’s morning colors. The rover has gained about 1 kilometer in elevation since it began climbing in 2014 and is expected to reach the yardangs’ base in 2027, where it can use its robotic arm to collect close-up data.
science.image_alt: NASA rover captures wind-carved Martian cliffs in dawn panorama

science.title: Brief contact with healthy clones restores bleached coral in lab tests
science.summary: Bleached coral fragments recovered after touching healthy, genetically identical fragments in Stanford University laboratory tests, according to a study published Oct. 14 in Science Advances. All five bleached fragments that touched healthy fragments regained health within seven weeks, while five kept a few millimeters
science.content: Bleached coral fragments recovered after touching healthy, genetically identical fragments in Stanford University laboratory tests, according to a study published Oct. 14 in Science Advances. All five bleached fragments that touched healthy fragments regained health within seven weeks, while five kept a few millimeters away died. Algae passed through fused tissue connections within three days, then multiplied rapidly inside the recovering coral. The method requires a healthy genetic match for each bleached coral, limiting its use across reefs. A separate Australian lab experiment tested heat-tolerant algae in two coral species. Researchers are also investigating how to deliver beneficial algae without requiring matching fragments to touch.
science.image_alt: Brief contact with healthy clones restores bleached coral in lab tests

science.title: Study estimates strong El Niño could cause 451,000 deaths
science.summary: Researchers with the Climate Impact Lab estimate that the unusually strong El Niño now unfolding could contribute to more than 451,000 deaths worldwide. Their September estimate has not yet been published in a peer-reviewed journal; they are preparing a paper detailing the methodology. The World Meteorological Organiza
science.content: Researchers with the Climate Impact Lab estimate that the unusually strong El Niño now unfolding could contribute to more than 451,000 deaths worldwide. Their September estimate has not yet been published in a peer-reviewed journal; they are preparing a paper detailing the methodology. The World Meteorological Organization expects the event to peak in December, while forecasts cited by the BBC say it could continue into 2027. Weather effects already vary sharply by region: Indonesia has recorded its worst wildfire season since 2015, while India’s monsoon rainfall is 13% below average. The mortality analysis warns that heat, floods, disease and food insecurity could compound the effects, with Nigeria, Indonesia, Sudan, India and Brazil among the countries expected to be hardest hit in the next six months.
science.image_alt: Study estimates strong El Niño could cause 451,000 deaths

science.title: ADHD linked to 70% higher mortality, medication tied to lower risk
science.summary: A review of 19 studies covering more than 15.9 million people found that people with ADHD had a 70% higher risk of death from any cause than those without the condition. The analysis also found higher mortality from suicide, injuries and natural causes, with a 90% increase for suicide and about 30% for natural causes.
science.content: A review of 19 studies covering more than 15.9 million people found that people with ADHD had a 70% higher risk of death from any cause than those without the condition. The analysis also found higher mortality from suicide, injuries and natural causes, with a 90% increase for suicide and about 30% for natural causes. Among people with ADHD, prescribed medication was associated with a 25% lower risk of death from any cause, but medication data came from only three of the 19 studies. The researchers cautioned that the review cannot establish that ADHD causes higher mortality or that medication prevents deaths. The studies also varied in population and context. The review was published in JAMA Network Open on Oct. 19, 2026.
science.image_alt: ADHD linked to 70% higher mortality, medication tied to lower risk

science.title: SpaceX Bandwagon-5 launch may create glowing plume over southeastern skies
science.summary: SpaceX is targeting a 6:30 a.m. launch Tuesday, Oct. 20, for its Bandwagon-5 satellite rideshare mission from Cape Canaveral, Florida. The rocket’s exhaust could appear as a glowing “space jellyfish” across parts of the Southeast. The launch was postponed from Monday because of unfavorable recovery weather, with a back
science.content: SpaceX is targeting a 6:30 a.m. launch Tuesday, Oct. 20, for its Bandwagon-5 satellite rideshare mission from Cape Canaveral, Florida. The rocket’s exhaust could appear as a glowing “space jellyfish” across parts of the Southeast. The launch was postponed from Monday because of unfavorable recovery weather, with a backup opportunity Wednesday if it does not go ahead Tuesday. The effect occurs when sunlight catches expanding rocket exhaust high above observers who are still in darkness. Visibility depends on the launch path and local conditions. The mission’s southeastward route favors central and southern Florida over North Carolina, while parts of coastal Louisiana and Mississippi may also have a view.
science.image_alt: SpaceX Bandwagon-5 launch may create glowing plume over southeastern skies

science.summary: California’s latest climate report warns that changing weather patterns could severely disrupt life in the state, according to a report published Oct. 19. The state’s Climate Change Assessment examines how those patterns affect the nation’s most populous state.

science.title: Euclid telescope discovers first new comet during galaxy survey
science.summary: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, C/2026 S1 (Euclid), in images taken from Sept. 16 to 24, 2026. The comet is about 1.3 billion kilometers from Earth and is expected to take thousands of years to complete an orbit. Mikko Pöntinen, a University of Helsi
science.content: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, C/2026 S1 (Euclid), in images taken from Sept. 16 to 24, 2026. The comet is about 1.3 billion kilometers from Earth and is expected to take thousands of years to complete an orbit. Mikko Pöntinen, a University of Helsinki researcher, found the moving object using software he developed to flag streaks in Euclid images. Follow-up observations from ground-based observatories helped confirm the discovery, and the Minor Planet Center officially designated the comet on Oct. 8. Euclid is designed to map billions of distant galaxies to study dark matter and dark energy. It generally avoids the dusty region where many Solar System objects are found, but the comet’s unusual path carried it through a survey field.
science.image_alt: Euclid telescope discovers first new comet during galaxy survey

science.title: Orionid meteor shower from Halley’s Comet to peak under bright Moon
science.summary: The annual Orionid meteor shower, produced by dust left by Halley’s Comet, is expected to peak overnight on Oct. 21-22, with 10 to 20 meteors an hour under dark skies. A bright waxing gibbous Moon will make fainter meteors harder to see, but viewing should improve after it sets. The shower is visible without a telescop
science.content: The annual Orionid meteor shower, produced by dust left by Halley’s Comet, is expected to peak overnight on Oct. 21-22, with 10 to 20 meteors an hour under dark skies. A bright waxing gibbous Moon will make fainter meteors harder to see, but viewing should improve after it sets. The shower is visible without a telescope in both hemispheres. In the UK, the Moon is expected to set at about 3 a.m. BST on Thursday, while cloud and rain could disrupt views in parts of the country. Australian astronomers recommend looking before dawn, after the Moon has set. The debris enters Earth’s atmosphere at about 66 kilometres per second.
science.image_alt: Orionid meteor shower from Halley’s Comet to peak under bright Moon

sports.title: FA Cup draw sends Leicester to sixth-tier Oxford City in first round
sports.summary: The 2026-27 FA Cup first-round draw sent Leicester City away to sixth-tier Oxford City, with 40 ties set for the weekend of November 7-8. League One and League Two clubs enter the competition in this round; Leicester, the 2021 winners, are appearing at this stage for the first time since 2008. Other fixtures include 20
sports.content: The 2026-27 FA Cup first-round draw sent Leicester City away to sixth-tier Oxford City, with 40 ties set for the weekend of November 7-8. League One and League Two clubs enter the competition in this round; Leicester, the 2021 winners, are appearing at this stage for the first time since 2008. Other fixtures include 2013 winners Wigan Athletic away to Boreham Wood and Sheffield Wednesday at Oldham Athletic. Robbie Savage’s Peterborough United will face Reading, where his son Charlie plays. Several matchups depend on qualifying replays, including a trip to Barnsley for either Aldershot Town or Tadley Calleva. The first-round matches are scheduled for the weekend of November 7-8, with the second-round draw expected on November 9.
sports.image_alt: FA Cup draw sends Leicester to sixth-tier Oxford City in first round

sports.summary: Tottenham Hotspur beat Coventry City 3-1 in London on Monday to claim their first Premier League win of the season after six winless league matches and move up to 16th place. sports.content: Tottenham Hotspur beat Coventry City 3-1 in London on Monday to claim their first Premier League win of the season after six winless league matches and move up to 16th place. James Maddison, making his first start in 536 days, put Spurs ahead; Omar Marmoush restored their lead after Jack Rudoni equalised, and Ben Davies scored in stoppage time. Dejan Kulusevski also returned from a long injury absence as a substitute. Manager Roberto De Zerbi said the result showed his players they could win and praised their attitude, although he said they had played better in some recent matches. Andy Robertson, Tosin Adarabioyo and Marmoush came off with apparent injuries, but De Zerbi said he did not think any were serious. Tottenham next play Chelsea on Saturday.

sports.content: Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds as her team beat the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 in San Francisco on Monday, October 19, tying the Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) Finals at one game apiece. Reese shot 10-for-16 and added three assists and two blocks after going scoreless in the second half of the opener. The Dream held Golden State to eight points over a 13-minute stretch spanning the third and fourth quarters, extending Atlanta's two-point halftime lead. The victory was Atlanta's first in the Finals after it lost all 10 games across three previous appearances. The best-of-seven series moves to Atlanta for Game 3 on Wednesday, October 21, and Game 4 on Saturday, October 24. Both games were moved to State Farm Arena to accommodate more fans. Both teams are seeking their first championship.

sports.content: England begin their campaign against Pakistan on Tuesday in Rawalpindi in the second match of a one-day international tri-series that also features Sri Lanka. Pakistan have two points after beating Sri Lanka by 37 runs in Sunday’s opener; the tournament’s top two teams will reach the October 31 final in Lahore. The series is part of England’s preparations for the 2027 Cricket World Cup. England head coach Brendon McCullum said the team would adapt to the conditions and opposition rather than follow a fixed plan. England’s four round-robin games run through October 29, with the final scheduled for October 31.

sports.content: UEFA, European football’s governing body, has given FIFA, its global counterpart, until November 2 to answer 42 questions and provide documents about FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s decisions and governance. The demand follows a FIFA Council meeting at which Infantino apologized for mistakes but, UEFA said, did not explain how key decisions were made or why the council was not consulted. The questions focus on FIFA Forward Enterprise, an abandoned proposal to sell private investors a stake in a company handling commercial rights to the World Cup and other competitions. UEFA also seeks records on the reversal of U.S. striker Folarin Balogun’s World Cup suspension, the FIFA Peace Prize awarded to President Donald Trump, Infantino’s compensation and FIFA’s election oversight. The proposed lead investor, Joshua Kushner, is the brother of Trump’s son-in-law. The deadline falls 16 days before the November 18 cutoff for presidential election nominations; the vote is scheduled for March 18. UEFA says it needs the answers before federations decide whether to back a challenger. The BBC reported that it had approached FIFA for comment, while The Associated Press reported that FIFA lawyers had described UEFA’s legal efforts over the investment proposal as harassment.

sports.content: Ukrainian tennis player and world No. 6 Elina Svitolina announced on Oct. 19 that she and former French tennis star Gaël Monfils are ending their marriage, saying the emotional toll of Russia’s war in Ukraine left her needing to rediscover herself outside the relationship. The pair married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter, Skai. Svitolina said they would continue to put their daughter first and remain a family. Svitolina described sleepless nights, doubts and a sense of losing herself, while crediting Monfils with supporting her. She said no one was to blame and asked for kindness and privacy as they adjust to the change. The announcement follows Monfils’ retirement from professional tennis, which the sport’s integrity agency lists as effective Oct. 5, ahead of a planned farewell at the Paris Masters. His retirement status means he cannot compete in sanctioned tournaments. Some reports linked the timing to the couple’s separation, but Svitolina did not say the events were connected.

sports.content: The Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series on Monday, winning the series 4-2 to advance to a World Series matchup with the Milwaukee Brewers. Tampa Bay’s third World Series appearance will be against a franchise that, like the Rays, has never won the championship. Milwaukee advanced by sweeping the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers. Rays starter Freddy Peralta allowed one run in 5⅓ innings, while Junior Caminero and Yandy Díaz each hit a two-run homer in the clinching win. Peralta, acquired by Tampa Bay at the trade deadline, was named American League Championship Series MVP after pitching in three games. Game 1 is scheduled for Friday, Oct. 23, at American Family Field in Milwaukee. The Brewers have home-field advantage after finishing with a league-best 103 regular-season wins; the Rays had 98. The best-of-seven series is the first since 1980 between two teams that had never won a World Series.

sports.title: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts expected to miss season after lung clots
sports.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season after doctors diagnosed deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs, the team and his agent, Nicole Lynn, said Monday. They said he is clinically stable and expected to make a full recovery with no lasting effects. He
sports.content: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season after doctors diagnosed deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs, the team and his agent, Nicole Lynn, said Monday. They said he is clinically stable and expected to make a full recovery with no lasting effects. He cannot participate in contact activities, including football, while taking blood-thinning medication. Specialists in London initially diagnosed Hurts with a superficial clot in his left calf. Further testing revealed deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, the Eagles said. The team has not announced a return date, but reports say treatment is expected to last at least three months, making a return this season unlikely. Hurts will remain with the team and continue conditioning while recovering. Backup quarterback Tanner McKee started Sunday against Carolina. Philadelphia’s next game is against the Dallas Cowboys on Oct. 26.
